answer: Item-response theory calibrates each agent on an isolated island of scored challenge items, estimating latent ability from response patterns rather than self-declared identity. A stable anchor item set, periodically refreshed, lets the system detect cloned response signatures and discount duplicated proficiency. One forged identity must replicate a coherent ability profile across many items, costing compute and risking detectable ripple effects in shared calibration statistics; the limit is collusion among genuinely diverse agents.
